title: Increasing dietary linoleic acid does not increase tissue arachidonic acid content in adults consuming Western-type diets: a systematic review
population: 36 published human studies in adults on Western-type diets reporting dietary linoleic acid and plasma, serum or erythrocyte phospholipid arachidonic acid
funder: This research was associated with the USDA Multistate Regional Research Project NC1039, and funded in part by the Tennessee Agricultural Experiment Station.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they have no competing interests.
result: Decreasing dietary linoleic acid by up to 90% was not significantly correlated with changes in plasma or serum phospholipid arachidonic acid (p = 0.39); increasing it up to sixfold showed no significant correlation (p = 0.72). Dietary gamma-linolenic and arachidonic acid were positively related to changes in arachidonic acid.
